title: Gen Z Flight Bookings Jump 60 Percent Ahead of Diwali, Cleartrip Finds
excerpt: Cleartrip's PeekABoo tracker shows hotel bookings up 135% for Diwali, with Udaipur, Gaya and Dimapur leading a shift toward Tier-2 and Tier-3 destinations.
body:
• Flight bookings by travellers aged 15-24 rose 60% ahead of Diwali, compared with 6% for ages 25-34, Cleartrip's PeekABoo tracker found.
  • Leisure hotel bookings rose 135% for Diwali; Udaipur hotel bookings rose 316%, Bengaluru 189% and Jaipur 174%.
  • Budget hotels led growth at 201%, followed by luxury at 162%, while bus bookings grew 80% for Delhi.
  • For diaspora families booking Diwali travel to India, the data points to smaller cities selling fastest — book Tier-2 destinations such as Udaipur, Gaya and Dimapur early, as those routes are seeing 59-98% flight growth.

Flight bookings by travellers aged 15 to 24 rose 60% ahead of Diwali, far outpacing the 6% rise among travellers aged 25 to 34, according to Cleartrip's PeekABoo travel trends tracker released on October 22. Women's share of bookings grew 44% over the same period.

The tracker describes a festive season moving deep into India's Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets, with travellers swapping traditional metro holidays for offbeat getaways and regional hubs. That shift, not just the headline Gen Z number, is the story in the data.

Hotels lead the festive boom

Leisure hotel bookings rose 135% for Diwali and 66% for Navratri, Cleartrip said. Udaipur's hotel bookings more than quadrupled, rising 316% for Diwali, while Bengaluru rose 189% and Jaipur 174%.

Growth ran across every price point. Budget stays rose 201%, luxury properties 162%, mid-range accommodation 148% and premium hotels 114%, according to the tracker as reported by Curly Tales in its coverage of the same Cleartrip data. The spread matters: this is not only a premium-travel surge and not only a budget one.

Smaller destinations, bigger growth

Flight bookings to Agatti grew 130%, to Gaya 98% and to Dimapur 80%. Udaipur recorded 59% flight growth, followed by Dibrugarh at 37%, Gorakhpur at 34%, Jabalpur at 29%, Imphal at 24% and Dehradun at 9%.

Bus travel, driven largely by people heading back to their hometowns for the festival, grew 80% for Delhi, 76% for Pune, 68% for Nagpur, 63% for Chennai and 57% for Mumbai.

Internationally, travellers looked beyond the usual hubs. Taipei led with 146% growth in flight bookings, followed by Cebu at 117%, Dublin at 110%, Phu Quoc at 106% and Osaka at 74%.

What this means for diaspora travellers

Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 this year. For non-resident Indians flying into India for the festival and then travelling onward domestically, the Cleartrip pattern is a practical warning: the tightest capacity is likely on routes and in hotels in smaller heritage and regional cities, not only in Delhi and Mumbai. Udaipur, Jaipur, Gaya and Dimapur all appear in both the hotel and flight growth lists.

Families combining an international arrival with a domestic leg should treat that domestic leg as the booking to lock first. The data also suggests younger travellers are booking independently in far larger numbers, which changes who in a family is making the travel decisions — and how early group plans need to be settled.

Cleartrip's tracker does not publish absolute booking volumes, so the percentages describe growth rates, not market size. Even with that caveat, the direction is consistent across flights, hotels and buses, and across budget and luxury tiers: festive travel in India this year is broader, younger and less metro-centred than the traditional Diwali homecoming story.
